opportunities.title: 974 CVEs in One Tuesday: Microsoft Just Set the Record Nobody Wanted
opportunities.why_now: Patch Tuesday hit an all-time high of 974 CVEs the same week Android shipped 180 more and Nvidia/AMD/Arm all issued advisories, making this the single biggest patch-load story of the year.
opportunities.angle: Digest/roundup with a 'what to patch first' triage list, tying in the Krebs and Dark Reading coverage plus the 'human bottleneck' angle on vuln overload

opportunities.title: Chrome's V8 Zero-Day Is Already Being Exploited — Here's Why Your Sandbox Isn't Saving You
opportunities.why_now: A Chrome V8 zero-day enabling code execution inside the sandbox is being actively exploited in the wild right now, days after four separate spy groups were caught sharing the same Chrome/Windows exploit kit.
opportunities.angle: Breaking-news brief with patch-now urgency, cross-reference the shared exploit kit story to show how fast these bugs get weaponized across threat actors

opportunities.title: CISA Confirms It: That WatchGuard Bug Is Now a Ransomware Delivery Mechanism
opportunities.why_now: CISA just confirmed active ransomware exploitation of a WatchGuard RCE flaw, landing the same week as confirmed Cisco Secure FMC and Fortinet exploitation — a perimeter-appliance pile-up.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor-focused explainer: 'edge devices are the new frontline,' with a quick-hit sidebar on the parallel Cisco and Fortinet exploitation stories

opportunities.title: Invisible Web Shell: F5 BIG-IP Malware Now Lives Only in Memory to Dodge Your Disk Scanner
opportunities.why_now: A newly disclosed F5 BIG-IP APM malware campaign injects a PHP web shell directly into memory specifically to evade disk-based detection, a notable evolution in enterprise persistence tradecraft.
opportunities.angle: Technical deep-dive on memory-resident malware and what it means for EDR/AV assumptions, framed as 'the scan that can't find what isn't there'

opportunities.title: 'sk-1234': The Default Admin Key Still Guarding 1 in 10 Exposed AI Gateways
opportunities.why_now: Nearly 10% of internet-exposed LiteLLM gateways were found still using the literal example admin key from the docs, a perfect, absurd case study in AI infrastructure security debt.
opportunities.angle: Snarky breach-inevitability piece — 'the password is literally in the README' — with a checklist for auditing LLM gateway configs
